propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Da nobis, quaesumus, Domine, imitari quod colimus: ut discamus et
inimicos diligere; quia ejus natalicia celebramus, qui novit etiam pro
persecutoribus exorare Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum:
Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

refused.hebrew: roman-1962 numbers Acts divergently (the Vulgate joins the two verses of Stephen's vision into one, its 7:55 carrying both the sight of the glory of God and the Ecce video caelos apertos that the Greek numbers 7:56, so its chapter 7 ends at 59 where the Greek ends at 60 and everything from the Greek's 7:56 stands one verse lower, its 7:59 also carrying the Greek's 8:1a. This day's four Acts citations do not all speak one system. The Lesson, printed 7, 54-59, is the Vulgate's - it ends at obdormivit in Domino, which the Vulgate numbers 7:59 and the Greek 7:60 - and it resolves to itself. The Alleluia, Offertory and Communion carry the Greek's numbers against chants whose words the Vulgate prints elsewhere. Video caelos apertos is the Vulgate's 7:55, not its 7:56, which is the crowd stopping its ears. Accipe spiritum meum is the Vulgate's 7:58, not its 7:59, which is ne statuas illis hoc peccatum. And 7:60 is past the end of the Vulgate's chapter altogether. propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Suscipe, Domine, munera pro tuorum commemoratione Sanctorum: ut, sicut
illos passio gloriosos effecit; ita nos devotio reddat innocuos. Per
Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat
in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
